reasons: F01, F02: material weakness from limited staffing/segregation of duties, so the control environment is weak, as is typical of a small reporting company
F03: no auditor ICFR attestation, so the weakness is self-assessed and controls get little outside checking
F04, F21: going-concern doubt plus a capital raise done or planned give management a strong reason to present results favourably
F05: auditor changed within two years, which reduces audit continuity and can signal friction or opinion shopping
F11: material related-party transactions give scope for non-arm's-length dealings and misclassification
F12, F13: largest customer is 41% of revenue and its receivables share is not disclosed, so revenue and collectability depend heavily on one customer
F20: incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS creates pressure on reported earnings
R19: operating cash flow is only 0.07x net income, so earnings are poorly backed by cash
R13: soft assets are 82% of total assets, which leaves large room for judgement in balance-sheet values
R09, R17: Beneish M-score (-3.06) is well below its -1.78 threshold and Dechow F-score (0.54) is below 1.0, so the composite models do not flag manipulation
R01, R18, R11, R12, R08, R10: receivables in line with sales, small receivable and inventory build-up, and negative accruals do not show the classic revenue-inflation pattern
F06, F07, F16, F17, F18, F19: no disagreements, restatements, investigations, litigation or covenant problems are disclosed
